 FDA classifies recall as potential for temporary or reversible adverse health consequences

 The FDA classified the recall as Class II, indicating possible temporary or medically reversible health effects.
 The cited reason is deviations from current good manufacturing practices.
 More than 4.3 million tubes of toothpaste — some made for children and others for sensitive teeth or whitening — have been recalled, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
 The recall was voluntarily initiated by the manufacturer, Pritam International Private Limited on Sept. 10, and FDA classified it as a Class II recall Oct. 19. Class II is a mid-level risk recall, where “use of or exposure to a violative product may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences or where the probability of serious adverse health consequences is remote.”
 Recalls with high health risk are categorized as Class I.
 While no specific explanation of what happened during manufacturing was given, the FDA reported that the toothpaste deviates from “Current Good Manufacturing Practice” that ensures acceptable drug quality.
 Seventeen toothpaste products are in the recall, but consumers should check the lot numbers on their toothpaste tubes, as not all lots are recalled.
 Related Food recalls are rising. Here's what to know Baby, children's items top list of increasing product safety recalls Included in the recall are many types of Brush Buddies Kids Toothpaste, which feature children’s character and brands like Barbie, Hot Wheels, My Little Pony and Crayola Silly Scents, among others.
 Some of the recalled toothpastes have flavors like vanilla or chocolate ice cream, bubble gum, cookies and cream and mint chocolate chip.
 2 Comments The recall also includes ARU cavity protection toothpaste and gum health toothpaste. Evo sensitive and advanced whitening toothpastes are also in the recall, as are some Brush Buddies Cavity Protection and Anti-Cavity Fluoride Toothpaste.
 The full list is available here on the FDA website.
 Consumers can throw the recalled product out or contact the retailer or manufacturer about returns or refunds.
 Pritam International Private Limited is headquartered in India and the products are distributed in the U.S. by Ashtel Studios Inc.
